extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying, avoiding, and responding to statutory and nonstatutory double patenting rejections (including interplay with prior art, 35 U.S.C. 121, terminal disclaimers, and joint research agreements) during patent prosecution and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.33 usage sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 8.33 must precede any one of form paragraphs 8.34 to 8.39 and must be used only ONCE in an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 8.33 as the lead paragraph before the specified subsequent form paragraphs; include it only once per Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: TC Director approval for Schneller-based rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: This form paragraph should only be used where approval from the TC Director to make a nonstatutory double patenting rejection based on In re Schneller has been obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and document TC Director approval before invoking the Schneller-based nonstatutory double patenting form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copending reference claim coverage requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this form paragraph only when the subject matter of the claim(s) is fully disclosed in, and covered by at least one claim of, another copending application (reference application) which is commonly owned, or where there is at least one common (joint) inventor or a common applicant (35 U.S.C. 118).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that the reference application both discloses and claims the subject matter and that common ownership/inventorship or common applicant status exists before applying the paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph bracket insertion instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: In bracket 3, insert the number of the reference application. In bracket 4, insert a description of the subject matter being claimed which is covered in the reference application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed form paragraph formatting: include the reference application number and a clear description of the overlapping subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 8.28.fti when ownership timing unclear (pre-AIA issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference application is currently commonly assigned but the prosecution file of the application under examination does not establish that the patentably indistinct inventions were commonly owned at the time the later invention was made, form paragraph 8.28.fti may be used in addition to this form paragraph to resolve any issues relating to priority under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) and/or (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When common ownership at the relevant time is not established by the file history, add 8.28.fti to address priority/derivation issues under pre-AIA rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA/FITF procedure when inventive entities differ
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications examined under first inventor to file (FITF) provisions of the AIA: If the reference application is to a different inventive entity and is commonly assigned with the application under examination, form paragraph 8.28.aia should additionally be used if there is no evidence of common ownership not later than the effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. 100(i) of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For AIA filings involving different inventive entities but common assignee, include 8.28.aia absent evidence of common ownership by the effective filing date; also make 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) or 103 rejections if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional double patenting rejection in reference application
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional double patenting rejection should also be made in the reference application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making a provisional double patenting rejection in the application under examination, ensure a corresponding provisional rejection is also made in the reference application to preserve proper prosecution posture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 102(e)/103(a) additional rejection (fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications being examined under pre-AIA (first to invent) law: If the reference application is prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) to the claimed invention, use form paragraph 7.21.01.fti to additionally make a rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) in the application with the later effective U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply form paragraph 7.21.01.fti to make the appropriate pre-AIA prior art rejections when the reference qualifies under 102(e); do not make/maintain such rejections if the reference is disqualified under pre-AIA 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer guidance & earlier-filed determination
rubrics_metrics.description: See MPEP §1490 for guidance regarding terminal disclaimers and withdrawal of nonstatutory double patenting rejections when these are the only rejections remaining. Note especially that priority or benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a) and (e) are not taken into account in determining which is the earlier-filed application for double patenting purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult MPEP §1490 for form and treatment of terminal disclaimers; when determining earlier-filed application for double patenting, do not factor priority/benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)/(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to design/plant vs utility situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting issues may be raised where an applicant has filed both a utility patent application (35 U.S.C. 111) and either an application for a plant patent (35 U.S.C. 161) or an application for a design patent (35 U.S.C. 171). In general, the same double patenting principles and criteria that are applied in utility-utility situations are applied to utility-plant or utility-design situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply double patenting principles to cross-type situations (utility vs design/plant) where appropriate; double patenting rejections in utility-plant situations may be made in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-utility double patenting may be found despite different claim focuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Although double patenting is rare in the context of utility versus design patents, a double patenting rejection of a pending design or utility application can be made on the basis of a previously issued utility or design patent, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that a design-utility double patenting rejection can be proper even if the utility claims concern internal construction and the design claims concern external surface configuration, depending on claim overlap or obvious variations (case law cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-to-claim comparison requirement for double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A double patenting rejection must rely on a comparison with the claims in an issued patent or pending application, whereas an anticipation or obviousness rejection based on the same patent or application under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 relies on a comparison with what is disclosed (whether or not claimed) in the same issued patent or pending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For double patenting, analyze only the claim scope of the reference; for 102/103, analyze the full disclosure of the reference. Do not conflate the two analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer cannot overcome prior art 102/103 rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer cannot be used to obviate a rejection based on prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 prior art, even though it may overcome a nonstatutory double patenting rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept a terminal disclaimer as a response to a 102 or 103 rejection; terminal disclaimers only address nonstatutory double patenting (subject to other requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make both prior art and double patenting rejections when supported
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner should make both a pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection and a double patenting rejection over the same reference when the facts support both rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the facts independently support both types of rejections, include both in the Office action; omission of an applicable rejection can affect whether a subsequent Office action may be made final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 103(c) disqualification effects
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-AIA applications (certain filing/pending dates): a commonly assigned/owned patent or application may be disqualified as pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art in a pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) rejection under 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reference is disqualified under pre-AIA 103(c), do not make or maintain 102(e)/103(a) rejections based on that disqualified prior art; nonetheless, the same reference may still support a double patenting rejection (claims-to-claims). See MPEP §2146 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant measures to avoid prior art effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignee/applicant may avoid a commonly assigned copending application's becoming prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) by measures such as filing on same day, merging copending applications into a single continuation-in-part and abandoning parents, or showing derivation under 37 CFR 1.132 or earlier invention date under 37 CFR 1.131(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise applicants of procedural and evidentiary options (simultaneous filing, CIP/abandon parent, derivation affidavits, 1.131/1.132 showings) to counter prior art effects where appropriate; see cited case law and MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA prior art exception (35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) / 102(c)) effects
rubrics_metrics.description: For AIA applications, subject matter in a commonly assigned/owned patent or application may be excepted as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) via 102(b)(2)(C); if 102(c) requirements are met, common ownership can be established by a joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the 102(b)(2)(C) exception properly applies, the disclosed subject matter is not available as prior art under 102(a)(2) and may not be used as a secondary reference in a nonstatutory double patenting rejection; however, claims of the excepted reference may still form the basis for a double patenting rejection. Do not make 102(a)(2)/103 rejections if the reference is excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint research agreement proof requirement before reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under both pre-AIA and AIA law, examiners cannot rely on the joint research agreement provisions to apply a nonstatutory double patenting rejection until applicant establishes the existence of a joint research agreement in accordance with 37 CFR 1.104(c)(4)(ii) or (c)(5)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require applicants to make the formal showing of a joint research agreement per 37 CFR before applying disqualification/exceptions based on JRA; do not assume JRA from assignment information alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition on certain double patenting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The third sentence of 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibits using a patent issuing on an application in which a requirement for restriction has been made (or an application filed as a result of such requirement) as a reference against any divisional application in a nonstatutory double patenting rejection, if the divisional application is filed before the issuance of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 35 U.S.C. 121 safe harbor only where the Office made the restriction requirement and the divisional was filed in response to that requirement prior to issuance; do not extend 121 protection to voluntarily filed divisionals or other nonconsonant situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 121 limited to divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition applies only where the Office has made a requirement for restriction and is limited to divisional applications; it does not afford protection to continuation-in-part (CIP) applications or all forms of continuing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply 121 protection to CIPs or applications not properly filed as divisional in response to an Office restriction requirement; review case law (Pfizer v. Teva, Janssen, G.D. Searle) for scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply — voluntary multiple filings (A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant voluntarily files two or more applications without a restriction requirement by the examiner. To obtain the benefit of 35 U.S.C. 121, claims must be formally entered, restricted in, and removed from an earlier application before they are filed in a divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple applications were filed voluntarily (no Office restriction requirement), 121 protection is not available. Ensure the procedural history shows the restriction requirement and proper claim handling to claim 121 protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply — loss of consonance (B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of the application under examination and claims of the other application/patent are not consonant with the restriction requirement, since the claims have been changed in material respects from the claims at the time the requirement was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether consonance (maintenance of the line of demarcation identified in the restriction requirement) exists; material changes destroying consonance remove 121 protection (case law cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply — withdrawal subject to allowance of linking claims (C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The restriction requirement was withdrawn because the requirement was written in a manner which made it clear to applicant that the requirement was made subject to the non-allowance of generic or other linking claims and such generic or linking claims are subsequently allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requirement was explicitly conditional and later the linking/generic claims are allowed, the original restriction effectively disappears and 121 protection may not apply in the same way; examine the withdrawal circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply — international ISA/IPEA only (D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for restriction (holding of lack of unity of invention) was only made in an international application by the International Searching Authority or the International Preliminary Examining Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply where the restriction was only an ISA/IPEA finding in the international phase; however, 121 may apply to national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371 where the restriction was made by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply — withdrawal before patent issues (E)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for restriction was withdrawn, in its entirety or in pertinent part, by the examiner before the patent issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A withdrawn restriction means the restriction requirement disappears; 121 protection tied to a restriction that disappears may not apply. Also, a restriction requirement in a parent may not carry over to a continuation unless reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply — identical claims/statutory double patenting (F)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of the second application are drawn to the 'same invention' as the first application or patent. In that case, a statutory double patenting rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 should be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are identical (same invention), bring a statutory double patenting rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 rather than relying on 121 to block a nonstatutory double patenting rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply — product/process restriction rejoined (G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a requirement for restriction between a product, a process of making the product, and a process of using the product was made subject to the non-allowance of the product and the product is subsequently allowed, any rejoined process claims should have the restriction withdrawn in accordance with 37 CFR 1.141(b) and MPEP §821.04.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If product claims are allowed and process claims are rejoined, withdraw the restriction and reassess applicability of 121; procedural follow-up per 1.141(b) and MPEP guidance is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 35 U.S.C. 121 prohibition does not apply — continuation-in-part (H)
rubrics_metrics.description: The second application is a continuation-in-part (CIP) application that includes claims restricted from the original application; 35 U.S.C. 121 does not afford protection to CIP applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply 121 protection to CIPs that incorporate restricted claims from an earlier application; CIPs are excluded by statute and case law (Pfizer, Janssen, G.D. Searle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding statutory double patenting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on the statutory type of double patenting can be avoided by amending the conflicting claims so that they are not coextensive in scope, or by canceling the conflicting claims in the pending applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory double patenting requires identical subject matter; amend or cancel conflicting claims (in all pending apps or all but one) to avoid such rejections. Terminal disclaimers are ineffective for statutory double patenting; 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits are inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding nonstatutory double patenting rejections (terminal disclaimer)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on a nonstatutory type of double patenting can be avoided by filing a terminal disclaimer in the application or proceeding in which the rejection is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File a terminal disclaimer meeting 37 CFR 1.321 requirements (including unenforceability provision if ownership ceases). Note limitations: terminal disclaimers filed after expiration of the reference patent are ineffective; disclaimers in the reference patent do not negate the propriety of a nonstatutory rejection in a later application; terminal disclaimer does not overcome 102/103 prior art rejections; 1.131 affidavits are inappropriate. See MPEP §1490 for forms and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer content and multiple references
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple conflicting patents and/or pending applications are applied in nonstatutory double patenting rejections made in a single application, it is necessary to disclaim the terminal part of any patent granted on the application which would extend beyond the expiration date of each one of the conflicting patents and/or applications; each commonly owned conflicting reference must be included in the terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid multiple terminal disclaimer fees and dual ownership problems, a single terminal disclaimer may be filed covering all conflicting commonly owned references (or based on a joint research agreement). Ensure 37 CFR 1.321(c)(3) and 1.321(d) requirements are met, including the provision that the patent is enforceable only while commonly owned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer procedural & legal effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer is a statement filed by an owner that disclaims or dedicates a portion of the entire term of all the claims of a patent; filing a terminal disclaimer to obviate a nonstatutory double patenting rejection is not an admission of the propriety of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 CFR 1.321 for formal requirements; a terminal disclaimer removes the double patenting rejection statutory effect but does not create a presumption on merits. Ensure any terminal disclaimer extends to continuations if intended; include unenforceability clause if ownership ceases as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consonance requirement for Section 121 protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonstatutory double patenting rejection may be avoided if consonance between the originally restricted inventions is maintained in a divisional application; consonance requires that the line of demarcation between the independent and distinct inventions identified by the examiner in the restriction requirement be maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the divisional maintains the original line of demarcation; loss of consonance removes Section 121 protection unless claims are patentably distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common issue date is not substitute for terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance upon a common issue date cannot effectively substitute for the filing of one or more terminal disclaimers in order to overcome a proper nonstatutory double patenting rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise applicants that a common issue date does not avoid potential dual ownership or enforceability problems; the Office cannot ensure common issue dates and terminal disclaimers remain the proper mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer unenforceability provision and JRA-specific requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminal disclaimers that overcome nonstatutory double patenting must include provisions (per 37 CFR 1.321) that the patent shall be unenforceable if it ceases to be commonly owned with the referenced application/patent; 1.321(d) sets requirements where the claimed invention resulted from activities within a joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure terminal disclaimers contain the enforceability clause and comply with special JRA rules in 1.321(d) when applicable; sample forms and further guidance are in MPEP §1490.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on use of 37 CFR 1.131 / 1.132 affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of a 37 CFR 1.131(a) affidavit in overcoming a statutory double patenting rejection or a double patenting rejection is inappropriate where the application is being rejected over a patent which claims the rejected invention; 37 CFR 1.132 may be used to show derivation in some circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept 1.131(a) affidavits as a substitute for addressing double patenting where claims are directed to substantially the same invention; consider 1.132 derivation showings where relevant and per MPEP §§715, 716.10, 718 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer timing and expiration limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed after the expiration of the reference patent is not effective to obviate a nonstatutory double patenting rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure terminal disclaimers are filed timely (before expiration of the reference patent) to be effective; late-filed disclaimers will not overcome nonstatutory double patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness definition under 35 U.S.C. 101 and effect on double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 101 prevents two patents from issuing on the same invention; 'same invention' means identical subject matter. Claims that differ (aside from minor wording differences) are not considered to be drawn to the same invention for double patenting purposes under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the statutory double patenting standard (identical subject matter) for 101 rejections; if claims are different though obvious variants, terminal disclaimers may be effective to overcome nonstatutory double patenting rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of disclaimer in reference patent on propriety of later rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclaimer filed in a reference patent that disclaims the earlier patentably indistinct claim(s) would have no impact on whether a nonstatutory double patenting rejection is proper in a patent that has, or an application for a patent that would have, a later expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not consider a disclaimer in a reference patent as automatically negating a double patenting rejection in a later application; evaluate claim overlap and terminal disclaimer requirements separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice when multiple provisional nonstatutory rejections exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appropriate provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection is made in each of two or more pending applications, the examiner should follow the practice set forth in MPEP §804, subsection I.B.1. and subsection VI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate treatment of multiple provisional rejections across related pending applications and follow the MPEP subsections for correct procedural handling prior to issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference claims may form basis for double patenting even if subject matter excepted as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of a reference excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) may still be the basis for a double patenting rejection, whether statutory or nonstatutory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when disclosure is excepted from being prior art, perform a claims-to-claims analysis to determine whether the reference's claims create double patenting issues; do not assume exception eliminates double patenting concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: When next Office action may be final after new nonstatutory rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant establishes that the relied upon reference is not prior art under the JRA provision or disqualifies it under pre-AIA 103(c), and a subsequent nonstatutory double patenting rejection based upon conflicting claims in the same reference is applied, the next Office action may be made final even if the applicant did not amend the claims (provided the examiner introduces no other new ground of rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that an amendment or applicant showing can prompt new double patenting rejections that may justify a final action if no other new grounds are added; ensure the new rejection was necessitated by applicant amendment or information disclosure within the relevant timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting public-policy rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of a terminal disclaimer in overcoming a nonstatutory double patenting rejection is in the public interest because it encourages disclosure of additional developments, earlier filing of applications, and earlier expiration of patents whereby the inventions become freely available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the public-policy underpinnings when evaluating terminal disclaimer acceptability; case law supports terminal disclaimers as promoting disclosure and limiting unwarranted patent term extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find sample terminal disclaimer forms and detailed requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements for a terminal disclaimer are set forth in 37 CFR 1.321. Sample forms of a terminal disclaimer, and guidance as to the filing and treatment of a terminal disclaimer, are provided in MPEP §1490.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 37 CFR 1.321 and MPEP §1490 for exact wording, fee requirements, and procedures for filing and processing terminal disclaimers.
